text:
Maya: Quick design sync — I'm proposing we phase-deprecate the ingress-facade v1 (the lightweight facade we added years ago) and consolidate clients onto gateway-surface v2. Want to outline a rollout that minimizes customer breakage: shim strategy, opt-in header, canaries, telemetry, rollback triggers. Thoughts?
Sam: +1 to consolidating, but we should avoid any change that forces SDK updates. Can we do header-based opt-in so old SDKs keep working? :thinking:
Jonah: header opt-in seems least disruptive. Also: need a compatibility shim for the transformation we do on rich attachments (v1->v2). We can implement as a sidecar that rewrites payloads.
Aleks: sidecar is fine but we should measure CPU/memory. If we do sidecar per-pod it might blow infra cost for Dedicated tenants. Alternative: edge rewrite cluster that translates on the fly.
Nadia: operationally we need clear SLOs: error rate, request latency, and token-per-request delta. If the shim adds >50ms p50 we need a plan B. Also add regression alerts tied to prompt tests.
Maya: agree. Proposal sketch: 1) opt-in header X-RW-Ingress-Compat: v1 2) transparent edge rewrite shim (central) for opt-in traffic 3) canary cohorts by tenant tag (beta -> heavy -> everyone) 4) fallback: if rewrite fails, route to v1 runtime with 503-metric + rollback.
Sam: +1. For SDK compatibility we should add a `compatibility` feature flag in SDKs that sets header automatically for a configurable window. Clients can flip it off when they upgrade.
Jonah: which metrics do we watch for automatic rollback? I suggest: a) increase in 5xx to >0.5% absolute over baseline b) p95 latency regression >150ms c) drop in token-success ratio (failed decoding) >1%.
Aleks: also watch cost-per-token delta; if central rewrite bursts network egress we could exceed Dedicated quotas. Track egress bytes per-minute for top tenants.
Maya: good list. Implementation notes: - edge shim will be written in Rust using our existing gateway plugin infra - small cache for attachments mapping - health-check endpoint /_compat/health returns rewrite stats
Aleks: rough config example for tenant cohorting (pseudo):
```
cohorts:
  - name: beta
    tenants: [acct-123, acct-987]
    header: X-RW-Ingress-Compat: v1
  - name: ramp-1
    percent: 10
```
Jonah: we should include a probe route that generates synthesized prompt sets to validate output parity. If divergence > threshold alert and pause rollout.
Nadia: ops runbook additions: - how to mute cohorts - emergency flag to route all compat header traffic to v1 runtime - postmortem template for regressions - telemetry dashboard link (add to runbook)
Maya: rollback triggers: any one of Jonah's three OR manual abort from SRE. On rollback we immediately flip routing to v1 runtime and mark rollout paused.
Sam: small implementation ask: put the compatibility header sniff & rewrite behind a feature flag so we can enable in prod for internal tenants first. Also add a tenant opt-out mechanism.
Aleks: implementation caveat: some clients use long polling websockets; shard translation can't block streaming. For streaming we should only rewrite headers/metadata, not body frames.
Jonah: noted — add a streaming-safe path in the shim (pass-through frames, transform handshake only).
Maya: action items: @Aleks prototype edge rewrite + health; @Jonah write parity probe harness + threshold; @Nadia draft runbook & dashboard widgets; @Sam coordinate SDK flag + default on for internal dev tenants. I'll slot a 30m follow-up tomorrow to review prototypes.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: compat-shim edge cluster -> canary cohort 'beta' at 2024-11-07T15:00Z (manual approval required).
Sam: thanks — I'll wire SDK opt-in flag and add tests. :thumbsup:
Nadia: adding runbook now.
Aleks: prototyping today, will push draft PR to infra/gateway-plugins.
Jonah: I'll shepherd parity harness and add smoke tests to the CI lane.
Maya: thanks team — aim to keep the deprecation silent for customers and give clear escape hatch. :rocket:
